verses.en: These are also proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.
verses.pt: Também estes são provérbios de Salomão, os quais transcreveram os homens de Ezequias, rei de Judá.
verses.en_web: These also are proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.
verses.en_bbe: These are more wise sayings of Solomon, copied out by the men of Hezekiah, king of Judah.

verses.en: It is the glory of God to conceal a thing: but the honour of kings is to search out a matter.
verses.pt: A glória de Deus é encobrir as coisas; mas a glória dos reis é esquadrinhá-las.
verses.en_web: It is the glory of God to conceal a thing, but the glory of kings is to search out a matter.
verses.en_bbe: It is the glory of God to keep a thing secret: but the glory of kings is to have it searched out.

verses.en: The heaven for height, and the earth for depth, and the heart of kings is unsearchable.
verses.pt: Como o céu na sua altura, e como a terra na sua profundidade, assim o coração dos reis é inescrutável.
verses.en_web: As the heavens for height, and the earth for depth, so the hearts of kings are unsearchable.
verses.en_bbe: The heaven is high and the earth is deep, and the hearts of kings may not be searched out.

verses.en: Take away the dross from the silver, and there shall come forth a vessel for the finer.
verses.pt: Tira da prata a escória, e sairá um vaso para o fundidor.
verses.en_web: Take away the dross from the silver, and material comes out for the refiner;
verses.en_bbe: Take away the waste from silver, and a vessel will come out for the silver-worker.

verses.en: Take away the wicked from before the king, and his throne shall be established in righteousness.
verses.pt: Tira o ímpio da presença do rei, e o seu trono se firmará na justiça.
verses.en_web: Take away the wicked from the king’s presence, and his throne will be established in righteousness.
verses.en_bbe: Take away evil-doers from before the king, and the seat of his power will be made strong in righteousness.

verses.en: Put not forth thyself in the presence of the king, and stand not in the place of great men:
verses.pt: Não reclames para ti honra na presença do rei, nem te ponhas no lugar dos grandes;
verses.en_web: Don’t exalt yourself in the presence of the king, or claim a place among great men;
verses.en_bbe: Do not take glory for yourself before the king, and do not put yourself in the place of the great:

verses.en: For better it is that it be said unto thee, Come up hither; than that thou shouldest be put lower in the presence of the prince whom thine eyes have seen.
verses.pt: porque melhor é que te digam: Sobe, para aqui; do que seres humilhado perante o príncipe.
verses.en_web: for it is better that it be said to you, “Come up here,” than that you should be put lower in the presence of the prince, whom your eyes have seen.
verses.en_bbe: For it is better to have it said to you, Come up here; than for you to be put down in a lower place before the ruler.

verses.en: Go not forth hastily to strive, lest thou know not what to do in the end thereof, when thy neighbour hath put thee to shame.
verses.pt: O que os teus olhos viram, não te apresses a revelar, para depois, ao fim, não saberes o que hás de fazer, podendo-te confundir o teu próximo.
verses.en_web: Don’t be hasty in bringing charges to court. What will you do in the end when your neighbor shames you?
verses.en_bbe: Do not be quick to go to law about what you have seen, for what will you do in the end, when your neighbour has put you to shame?

verses.en: Debate thy cause with thy neighbour himself; and discover not a secret to another:
verses.pt: Pleiteia a tua causa com o teu próximo mesmo; e não reveles o segredo de outrem;
verses.en_web: Debate your case with your neighbor, and don’t betray the confidence of another;
verses.en_bbe: Have a talk with your neighbour himself about your cause, but do not give away the secret of another:

verses.en: Lest he that heareth it put thee to shame, and thine infamy turn not away.
verses.pt: para que não te desonre aquele que o ouvir, não se apartando de ti a infâmia.
verses.en_web: lest one who hears it put you to shame, and your bad reputation never depart.
verses.en_bbe: Or your hearer may say evil of you, and your shame will not be turned away.

verses.en: A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in pictures of silver.
verses.pt: Como maçãs de ouro em salvas de prata, assim é a palavra dita a seu tempo.
verses.en_web: A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver.
verses.en_bbe: A word at the right time is like apples of gold in a network of silver.

verses.en: As an earring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, so is a wise reprover upon an obedient ear.
verses.pt: Como pendentes de ouro e gargantilhas de ouro puro, assim é o sábio repreensor para o ouvido obediente.
verses.en_web: As an earring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, so is a wise reprover to an obedient ear.
verses.en_bbe: Like a nose-ring of gold and an ornament of the best gold, is a wise man who says sharp words to an ear ready to give attention.

verses.en: As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, so is a faithful messenger to them that send him: for he refresheth the soul of his masters.
verses.pt: Como o frescor de neve no tempo da sega, assim é o mensageiro fiel para com os que o enviam, porque refrigera o espírito dos seus senhores.
verses.en_web: As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, so is a faithful messenger to those who send him; for he refreshes the soul of his masters.
verses.en_bbe: As the cold of snow in the time of grain-cutting, so is a true servant to those who send him; for he gives new life to the soul of his master.

verses.en: Whoso boasteth himself of a false gift is like clouds and wind without rain.
verses.pt: como nuvens e ventos que não trazem chuva, assim é o homem que se gaba de dádivas que não fez.
verses.en_web: As clouds and wind without rain, so is he who boasts of gifts deceptively.
verses.en_bbe: As clouds and wind without rain, so is one who takes credit for an offering he has not given.

verses.en: By long forbearing is a prince persuaded, and a soft tongue breaketh the bone.
verses.pt: Pela longanimidade se persuade o príncipe, e a língua branda quebranta os ossos.
verses.en_web: By patience a ruler is persuaded. A soft tongue breaks the bone.
verses.en_bbe: A judge is moved by one who for a long time undergoes wrongs without protest, and by a soft tongue even bone is broken.

verses.en: Hast thou found honey? eat so much as is sufficient for thee, lest thou be filled therewith, and vomit it.
verses.pt: Se achaste mel, come somente o que te basta, para que porventura não te fartes dele, e o venhas a vomitar.
verses.en_web: Have you found honey? Eat as much as is sufficient for you, lest you eat too much, and vomit it.
verses.en_bbe: If you have honey, take only as much as is enough for you; for fear that, being full of it, you may not be able to keep it down.

verses.en: Withdraw thy foot from thy neighbour’s house; lest he be weary of thee, and so hate thee.
verses.pt: Põe raramente o teu pé na casa do teu próximo, para que não se enfade de ti, e te aborreça.
verses.en_web: Let your foot be seldom in your neighbor’s house, lest he be weary of you, and hate you.
verses.en_bbe: Let not your foot be frequently in your neighbour's house, or he may get tired of you, and his feeling be turned to hate.

verses.en: A man that beareth false witness against his neighbour is a maul, and a sword, and a sharp arrow.
verses.pt: Malho, e espada, e flecha aguda é o homem que levanta falso testemunho contra o seu próximo.
verses.en_web: A man who gives false testimony against his neighbor is like a club, a sword, or a sharp arrow.
verses.en_bbe: One who gives false witness against his neighbour is a hammer and a sword and a sharp arrow.

verses.en: Confidence in an unfaithful man in time of trouble is like a broken tooth, and a foot out of joint.
verses.pt: Como dente quebrado, e pé deslocado, é a confiança no homem desleal, no dia da angústia.
verses.en_web: Confidence in someone unfaithful in time of trouble is like a bad tooth, or a lame foot.
verses.en_bbe: Putting one's faith in a false man in time of trouble is like a broken tooth and a shaking foot.

verses.en: As he that taketh away a garment in cold weather, and as vinegar upon nitre, so is he that singeth songs to an heavy heart.
verses.pt: O que entoa canções ao coração aflito é como aquele que despe uma peça de roupa num dia de frio, e como vinagre sobre a chaga.
verses.en_web: As one who takes away a garment in cold weather, or vinegar on soda, so is one who sings songs to a heavy heart.
verses.en_bbe: Like one who takes off clothing in cold weather and like acid on a wound, is he who makes melody to a sad heart.

verses.en: If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink:
verses.pt: Se o teu inimigo tiver fome, dá-lhe pão para comer, e se tiver sede, dá-lhe água para beber;
verses.en_web: If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat. If he is thirsty, give him water to drink:
verses.en_bbe: If your hater is in need of food, give him bread; and if he is in need of drink, give him water:

verses.en: For thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head, and the LORD shall reward thee.
verses.pt: porque assim lhe amontoarás brasas sobre a cabeça, e o Senhor te recompensará.
verses.en_web: for you will heap coals of fire on his head, and Yahweh will reward you.
verses.en_bbe: For so you will put coals of fire on his head, and the Lord will give you your reward.

verses.en: The north wind driveth away rain: so doth an angry countenance a backbiting tongue.
verses.pt: O vento norte traz chuva, e a língua caluniadora, o rosto irado.
verses.en_web: The north wind produces rain; so a backbiting tongue brings an angry face.
verses.en_bbe: As the north wind gives birth to rain, so is an angry face caused by a tongue saying evil secretly.

verses.en: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman and in a wide house.
verses.pt: Melhor é morar num canto do eirado, do que com a mulher rixosa numa casa ampla.
verses.en_web: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, than to share a house with a contentious woman.
verses.en_bbe: It is better to be living in an angle of the house-top, than with a bitter-tongued woman in a wide house.

verses.en: As cold waters to a thirsty soul, so is good news from a far country.
verses.pt: Como água fresca para o homem sedento, tais são as boas-novas de terra remota.
verses.en_web: Like cold water to a thirsty soul, so is good news from a far country.
verses.en_bbe: As cold water to a tired soul, so is good news from a far country.

verses.en: A righteous man falling down before the wicked is as a troubled fountain, and a corrupt spring.
verses.pt: Como fonte turva, e manancial poluído, assim é o justo que cede lugar diante do ímpio.
verses.en_web: Like a muddied spring, and a polluted well, so is a righteous man who gives way before the wicked.
verses.en_bbe: Like a troubled fountain and a dirty spring, is an upright man who has to give way before evil-doers.

verses.en: It is not good to eat much honey: so for men to search their own glory is not glory.
verses.pt: comer muito mel não é bom; não multipliques, pois, as palavras de lisonja.
verses.en_web: It is not good to eat much honey; nor is it honorable to seek one’s own honor.
verses.en_bbe: It is not good to take much honey: so he who is not looking for honour will be honoured.

verses.en: He that hath no rule over his own spirit is like a city that is broken down, and without walls.
verses.pt: Como a cidade derribada, que não tem muros, assim é o homem que não pode conter o seu espírito.
verses.en_web: Like a city that is broken down and without walls is a man whose spirit is without restraint.
verses.en_bbe: He whose spirit is uncontrolled is like an unwalled town which has been broken into.
